utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. I think under those circumstances -- unless there's any specific reason you'd like to explain to us in private session, but then a lot of other matters have to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you were residing in -- in the Netherlands, did you receive any media reports concerning the level of fighting? I'm talking now about the period of time before -- immediately before you went to Tirana or Albania.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: During the time I was in the Netherlands, there were reports on the Albanian satellite television, but I also heard about the fighting during the meetings that were held in the clubs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you provided with any information as to the frequency of -- of clashes or the intensity of clashes during that period of time, when you were speaking to your -- to friends in the clubs?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: In the meetings in those clubs, we heard presentations about the situation in Kosovo and the fighting that was occurring at the time. But as to the intensity, I don't think I received any information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now go back to the period of time that you were in -- living in Tirana prior to your crossing the border. You've said that you received information from some of your -- from some of your colleagues. What precise sort of information were you receiving? Could you give the Trial Chamber a bit more detail? Were you receiving information as to where the fighting was occurring and what sort of fighting was going on?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: At that time, as I was told by my colleagues and the media, there were reports about fightings in several territories, but as far as to where exactly, I did not have concrete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you -- did your colleagues provide you with any detail as to the nature of the fighting, whether it was full-scale clashes or hit-and-run type episodes or the numbers of men involved, any of that sort of information?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: No. At that time I was not told where this -- the fighting was occurring. There were small clashes, as far as I know, but not -- I don't know any concrete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. You've told us already that you crossed the border around the 28th of May, 1998, and you went into Kosovo. At some later point, did you ever go to the Dukadjini area; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: After I entered Kosova on the 28th of May, 1998, the whole group I was part of went up to the General Staff, and then there at the General Staff, we were given our functions and posts --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: -- I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If I can just interrupt you. What I'm trying to do is get you to focus on a period of time now. Okay? All I want you to tell me is did you - after you crossed into Kosovo at some later point - did you go to the Dukadjini area; and if so, when was that trip, approximately?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, I was there in mid-July --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: -- the first time and then in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So we now know that there was a period of time when you crossed into Kosovo late May. You were in Kosovo for about a month and a half, and then later you went to the Dukadjini Zone, correct -- Dukadjini area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So now I'm going to ask you some questions about that period of time between that visit -- between your entering Kosovo and that visit. And I'm not going to -- and I'll later ask you some questions about the visit. In the period of time between late May and mid-July, what were your -- what were you responsible for and what were your activities?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: From the end of May up to mid-July, my duties were the duties of an officer in the operational department of the General Staff. I was an officer responsible for the development of the KLA, and my duties included giving advice, training, and also the staffs and the units that were created. In the beginning, I was asked to go and give advice and train in the areas where there were units from Mitrovica to Klina. I visited the KLA in various positions, defence positions they had occupied, and also giving them advice about the coordination between the units, and I was also responsible for the development of the military structure that had to be developed in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there a structure already existing from what you saw and observed in that period of time? I know that you said there had to be a development of a military structure in the future. My question is: Was -- that may be so, but was there already a structure that you could see or some sort of structure?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: At the time I went there, I found some structures, but they were mostly local staffs, local headquarters in the territories that I visited. But there wasn't a proper military structure containing, for example, structures like commander and the other structures lower than the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you set [Realtime transcript read in error "said"] about proposing and re-arranging these local staffs or headquarters into something that was more comprehensive and more coherent?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you provide weapons training to various KLA staffs?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes. During that period, I gave advice but also this advice comprised the way the training should be held. But I did not personally participate in the training.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- can you help the Trial Chamber with any figures concerning the number of men available to the KLA, fighting men available to the KLA, in Kosovo during this period of time, between late May and mid-July 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many there were, because I did not have full information. But there were KLA soldiers in the whole of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Page 49, line 15, there is a mistranscription of what was, in fact, a leading question. The question as asked was: "And you set about proposing and re-arranging these local staffs or headquarters into something that was more comprehensive and more coherent?" Now, that is -- rather a broad, but potentially important, general statement and the witness was persuaded to agree with it. I wonder if Mr. Di Fazio could now be asked, please, to elaborate on what is meant or what the witness means by re-arranging local staffs and headquarters into something more comprehensive and more coherent and what this witness's role was in re-arranging local staffs and headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can understand that Mr. Emmerson would be interested in that matter, and of course that's a matter that he can raise in cross-examination, but I've got a time constraint on me, if Your Honours please, and I need to get on with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Di Fazio, if you would like the Chamber to understand the testimony well where he said there was no command structure, et cetera, and if at the same time you are talking about re-arranging of headquarters, a headquarters of course suggests that there is a kind of a command structure because there is a headquarter usually --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you find the people are then -- but the witness also said there was no command structure. The witness testified about logistic departments, but it was early, it was elsewhere. So to say -- if you leave it like it is, of course it's your time. The suggestion might, if followed, might give some further information which might assist the Chamber in understanding the, in this respect, not-entirely-clear evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll certainly do my level best to assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm only concerned -- I'm not sure, with respect, that Mr. Di Fazio quite has the freedom of choice that he assumes because he's put a leading question the meaning of which remains unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I left it -- as a matter of fact, I did not say anything about the technicality. Of course I would expect you to oppose against the question if it's there, but of course a leading question comprising of certain of -- of several elements and then just a yes, where in the context certainly the question is not entirely clear is not something that would best assist the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the structure of local staffs or local headquarters in the territories that you saw and observed? What sort of structure did you see?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: At the time, in my visit to this territories from Mitrovica to Klina, I went to local staffs, which means that there was a command at the village level or neighbourhood level, but there was no command structure, there was no proper military command structure with a proper ranking and so on. There were groups that were not coordinated with each other. And that's why I went there, to give advice and expertise how to coordinate. I -- what I did was that I made a proposal to the operational department, and from there on we continued with a development of a proper army with a creation of squads, platoons, companies, battalions, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The commands that you observed at village level, what sort of structures did they in particular have in place, any that you saw?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: What I saw was that in the local staff they had a commander, but they had no structure, no hierarchy or no further groups to command such as squads and companies and so on. When I met these people, these were only groups, simple groups of people, 10 to 20 soldiers that had gotten together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you saw no local commands larger than that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: No, not in that period when I was visiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And just tell us of the areas that you visited in that period of time. Could you just remind us again?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The areas that I visited, I went from Mitrovica towards Klina, which is mostly a territory under Drenica municipality. So I went to these areas and gave them advice about further developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And in that period of time, late May to mid-July 1998, did you go to the Dukadjini area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, mid-July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. But before that you hadn't -- had you gone to the area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'd like to now ask you about, that is your visit in July of 1998 to the area. At about this time, what was your rank, or rather, position within the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: During this period, when I went to visit the Dukagjini area, I got the function of the director of operational department of this General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what did that -- what did that job actually entail? What were you responsible for?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Well, operational responsibilities in the General Staff of the KLA, which included development, training, and operations on the ground, further development of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when you -- when you visited the Dukagjini area, how long before that had you received that appointment to that position as director of the operational department?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was only the day before or two days before I went to -- on this visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was your purpose, your exact purpose, in going to this area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When we went to the area, we went together with other members of the General Staff. We met in Jablanica with Ramush Haradinaj. In addition to this meeting, I also wanted to get acquainted with the territory and the area, so I wanted to stay for a further few days in order to learn about the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did -- did you have an idea that you -- let me withdraw that and let me rephrase that. Were you intending to visit any military structure in Dukadjini --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is an extraordinarily difficult question to follow, unless -- if Mr. Di Fazio is referring to a physical structure of some kind, he should spell out what physical structure he's referring to. If he's referring to some sort of organisational structure, then he ought to put a proper question, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you intending to visit any sort of organisational structure, military organisational structure, in the area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: My visit was -- the purpose of my visit was to examine the commands and lower down, and in this case in the Dukagjin Zone. The meeting held at Ramush staff, who was the commander of the zone at the time, then we wanted to see how much the command was developed. I wanted to learn about the terrain, to get acquainted with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You've said that the meeting was held at the Ramush staff. What's the Ramush staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I didn't say Ramush staff but in Jabllanice, between the General Staff, but in the territory of Ramush Haradinaj. In the operational zone which I learned while I was going there; namely, that Ramush Haradinaj was the commander of the operational zone, and that a meeting was going to be held between the zone commander and the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Who provided you with this information that Ramush Haradinaj was the commander of the operational zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The General Staff, the former directors of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you got to the area, from what you saw and observed, was that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I'm not clear about the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you arrived at the area, from what you saw and observed, was the information that Ramush Haradinaj was the commander of the operational zone correct information?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I arrived there and held the meeting, we were told that he was the commander of the operational zone. And during my visit, I stayed there for three days, I couldn't visit the entire territory to find out exactly where his command reached, how far his command reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us that you -- the General Staff or former directors of the General Staff provided you about that information -- about Mr. Haradinaj. And you've also just told us now when you arrived there was a meeting and we were -- and you said: "We were told that he was the commander of the operational zone." Who told you when you arrived there and the meeting was held that Ramush Haradinaj was the commander of the operational zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The members of the staff, the former director of the operation department, Rexhep Selimi and Sokol Bashota. On the way there, I was told that Ramush Haradinaj was the zone commander and that we were supposed to hold a meeting with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, did you -- I think you earlier said that you did meet with Mr. Haradinaj. Can you recall where precisely that was when you first met him?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: For the first time I met him in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's covered elsewhere. You don't have to worry about that. I'm now talking about this July -- July visit. Okay? I mean, the July of 1998 visit to the Dukadjini Zone. And where did you first meet him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I met him in Jabllanice, where the meeting was actually held, the meeting of the General Staff, with the zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And did he introduce himself to you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When the meeting started, I wasn't present at that actual moment because I was visiting the units. So I arrived there when the meeting was underway. So I don't know how he introduced himself initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there any other commanders of the -- of the zone at the meeting when you arrived, any other subordinates?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: To my recollection, there were the members of the General Staff, Ramush Haradinaj, myself, and others whose names I cannot recall precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the period of time that you were there, did you ever meet any deputy commanders?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: During that time, I met in the -- Sali Veseli, who was in Dukagjin command, he was Chief of Staff, if I am not mistaken. At least this is how he introduced himself to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just want to be precise about that. Sali Veseli who's the Chief of Staff of which particular command or entity?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Of the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber where -- when you first met him?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: For the first time? I saw him in July in the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where -- where precisely was that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: In the General Staff, I said, in Berisha Mountain. That was where part of the General Staff was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Apart from that meeting in the Berisha Mountains, did you see him again?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him frequently, because he was in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see him during this trip in July that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, because he was a member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And again, if you would just be so kind as to clarify which particular staff you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: At this moment, I'm talking -- because when I first met him, he was chief of the finance division, but he was a member of the General Staff. And as such in this capacity, we went together to the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. You travelled together with him to -- to the area. Is that correct? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, with Lahi and the other members of the General Staff who participated in the meeting: Hashim Thaqi, Jakup Krasniqi, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he told any position in the Dukadjini command that you have referred to?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: As far as I was informed from the staff, before he was a commander of Dukagjini Zone. When I met him, he was performing the duty of director of the finance department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And is that the director of the finance department of the KLA General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman named Nazmi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see him during this visit in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I don't remember. I remember I saw him in 1998, then I saw him in August. And when I saw him, he was deputy commander of the zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I apologise for being pedantic, deputy commander of which zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Of the Dukagjini Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you now to concentrate on the -- the first day that you were in this area. You've already spoken briefly about a meeting that you had at which a number of personalities were present. Did you -- did you conduct any inspections of any KLA forces or KLA equipment in the area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: After the meeting we held in Jabllanice, I went to Gllogjan together with Ramush and Sali Veseli was also there. In the evening when we arrived in Gllogjan, we rested there for a while in a house. We spent the night there. On the next day, I inspected the units of the KLA in Gllogjan. Then I visited two positions in the vicinity of Gllogjan where there were anti-artillery machine-guns, 12.7 millimetres. I was together with Ramush when we visited these positions. Then I visited in Irzniq, Prilep -- I'm talking of the second day. Then we returned to Gllogjan in -- after lunch, in the afternoon, with Sali Veseli. I visited Shaptej village until the evening of that day. Then in the evening I asked to visit the territory of Reka e Keqe. During that night we visited the territory of Reka e Keqe --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now I'd just like to interrupt you there if I may. I'd like to elicit some more details about what you just told us. You say that you got to Gllogjan and you rested in a house. Whose house did you -- which house was this?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: It was a house near the command belonging to the family of Ramush, at least this is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where was the command -- where was it actually located, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The command was located in a house belonging -- close to Ramush's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You also mentioned that you inspected some units in Gllogjan -- sorry, your actual phrase was: "The next day," and this is after you had rested, you "inspected units of the KLA in Gllogjan?" Can you give the Trial Chamber an understanding of what these units were, how big they were?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I said that on the next day after arriving in Gllogjan we visited the command, when I was there, there were not only the Gllogjan units, there were also other units or groups which passed from Kosova to Albania, from Albania to Kosova. So I cannot give you an exact figure. Then we visited these two points, that I mentioned, of the anti-artillery positions. Then we returned to Gllogjan, but I cannot give you the exact number of units because I didn't know that at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, may I ask one question to form a better understanding of the testimony of the witness. Mr. Zyrapi, you told us in your testimony that when you visited these territories from Mitrovica to Klina, that you found no command structure, no proper military command, no proper ranking, et cetera, just groups. Now, was what you observed there different from what you found in the zone over which Mr. Haradinaj was commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of my visit in Gllogjan and the other places I mentioned, and earlier visits in other zones from Mitrovice to Kline, there were almost the same structures, structures that were not typical of military -- proper military structures, mostly consisting of groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, you are talking about commanders, sub-commanders, you're talking about anti-artillery positions, which -- visiting units, headquarters, which, well, sounds as if there was at least a military structure which had some good organisation, at least division of tasks. You also earlier said that -- talking about the others' areas, not more than 10 to 20 people in a group. It's difficult for me to understand where, on the one hand you give a picture as if some kind of unorganised local groups, and at the same time you're talking -- you're saying that it's not different from that about commanders, sub-commanders, headquarters, units you visited, specific tasks given to those units, which I have some difficulty to reconcile. Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could. In answer to the question about the differences between these zones, in July, mid-July, when efforts started to re-organise commands in the level of zones and staffs, when I went to Gllogjan these efforts were underway to form the command. There was a Chief of Staff, there was commander and members of the staff, but when we visited the territories at the local level, they were not militarily formed in terms of units that were coordinated among themselves. But where the command was that we visited and that we visited those arms that I mentioned, 12.7 machine-guns, they too were at the phase of being re-organised and being incorporated in the zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, what you described is what you found, as far as I understand, your first visit to this zone. So before you ever went there, coming there for the first time you find already this -- well, more or less organised structure -- yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The language at this stage may be a matter to which very particular care needs to be paid. We're dealing with a chronology of events, and the witness's evidence - and I'm very happy to explore it in more detail by reference to documentation in cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do that and if that would give a clear picture, then I desist at this moment from asking further questions, and if any question then remains I'll put them to the witness at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not discouraging Your Honour, but the witness's evidence is that the command structure was in a phase of development.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's not discuss it at this moment. We'll hear further evidence if the question remains then I'll put it to the witness. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned the anti-aircraft guns. Who took you to see these anti-aircraft guns?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I didn't say "guns," I said "machine-guns," 12.7 millimetres, anti-aircraft guns -- machine-guns, I went together with Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you provide advice on -- let me withdraw that? What did you do -- what did you do when you went to inspect them? What was the purpose of the visit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The purpose of my visit was to see how the weapons were positioned, where they were placed, in the proper place, and to see how the soldiers were doing, whether they were properly trained in the use of such weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know how many soldiers were manning those particular weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I visited them at the time that I was there, there were about five or six people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they members of any units as far as you could ascertain?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, they were members of the Gllogjan unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you know that? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I was there with Ramush, visiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned visits to other villages in the area, including Rznic and Saptej I think is the pronunciation. Who arranged to take you to those -- to those areas -- to those villages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, could we first try to -- to better understand the last answer given by the witness. You said, Mr. Zyrapi: "They were members of the Gllogjan unit," you gave that as a fact. Mr. Di Fazio then asked you: "How did you know that? Who told you that?" Which already suggested that you heard it from someone. But apart from that, he then said: "I was there with Ramush visiting," did you intend to say that Ramush told you that these were members of his unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned in your evidence visits to other areas and villages during your -- this brief tour. Who made arrangements to take you to these other locations?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: After Gllogjan, as I said, I visited Irzniq, together with Ramush. There we met the commander of the Irzniq unit, local commander, Shemsedin Qeku, and we visited Togeri, the rapid intervention unit, which was situated in the vicinity of the school, I think 100 or 150 metres from the school. After this visit, we continued on to Prilep, where there, too, we met the local commander of the village, Maliq Ndrecaj, I think was his name. And there we went also together again with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Now, you've told us where you went and some of the people you saw, and I'll ask you some more questions about that in a moment. But what I'd like to know is: How did you arrive at the decision to go to these places? How was that worked out, on what basis? Why Rznic? Why Saptej? Why any of these other places? Why speak to those particular individuals? I'd just like to know how -- how it was brought about.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I went there to visit the units. That's why I asked to visit these places and these units to see how the level of their organisation was, how well they were organised. And then after my demand to go and visit them, Ramush made it possible for me to go and we went together, as I said, to visit the places I mentioned, given the time I had at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to the visit to Rznic, and you mentioned the rapid intervention unit, did you -- did you already know of the -- of the existence of a rapid intervention unit in Rznic and ask to be taken there; or were you informed once you arrived in the area? That's essentially what I'd -- what I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I didn't have any prior knowledge of such a unit. When I arrived there, I learned that there is such a unit as that of the rapid intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And who provided you with information into -- in relation to the existence of that particular unit and its location?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you earlier said to the witness -- mentioned visit to Rznic and Saptej. Have I missed something? I remember that he said Prilep and Rznic. I didn't hear him -- and I tried to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I focused on one particular place, Rznic, and I'll deal with the others --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but where did the witness say that he visited Saptej? I couldn't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have mentioned visits to other villages in the area, including Rznic and Saptej, you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I thought -- unless I'm wrong, I thought he did mention that place, but if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it was a search on today, he said Prilep, but I didn't hear him say Saptej.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can I ask him? I'll ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you attend, during the course of your tour, at a village called Saptej?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The village of Shaptej, yes. I went there together with Sali Veseli.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness can be -- we'll settle this up now. The witness can be shown 65 ter 1306, which is -- consists of two pages and two maps, being maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P119, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Is it possible to flip it? Thank you. And possible to enlarge it a bit, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, Witness, Mr. Zyrapi, first of all, that's an electronic representation of a map. Are they your markings?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, I visited in the area when I was there in Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And there's some numbering there. Number 1 is near to the village of Jablanica; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes. Number 1 is Jabllanice village, where I was the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And number 2 is, I think, Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you see on either side of Gllogjan there are two markings with, I think, the number 3 next to both of those markings. What do those two markings represent?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: As I said earlier, this represents the positions with the anti-aircraft guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And number 5, does that indicate the village of Rznic that you attended, you went to?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, Irzniq village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. And number 6 is the village of -- it's clear, it's the village of Prilep. Did you also go and carry out inspections in Prilep?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to that village as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I wonder if the -- if the map can be raised just a little bit more so that we see the bottom part. We see a dotted line there I'm going to ask -- okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you also see a dotted line going down through -- past an area called -- or a place called Babaloc and then crossing over the -- the road that runs between -- or runs from Decani southwards. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What does that dotted line -- what does that path represent?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: It represents the way to Reka e Keqe. The route -- the route I followed to go to Reka e Keqe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please, I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection? It has got a number already; therefore, it's admitted into evidence. By the way, Mr. Di Fazio, I stand corrected as far as the witness earlier mentioning Saptej. It was in his recent answer that he referred to Prilep, but some nine pages prior to that he mentioned Saptej. The problem is that it was spelt in a different way. So when I searched for it, I missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I just -- has now the two maps document been admitted or just the first map?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Are you going to come back to the second map?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to the second one in due course. I think they need separate -- separate numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It is one. One and the same number, or is it in separate numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, there's one that I've just taken the witness through which also bears the word "Annex A," and that's now got a number, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Only the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Only the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's a combined piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, it was originally as part of the statement, if Your Honours please, but I'm going to deal with the second map in a separate portion of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour for -- for covering that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to ask you about your visits to some of these -- to these villages, and in particular I want to ask you about Rznic. You've already mentioned that you went there and you -- and you went there with Mr. Haradinaj and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time in order to avoid whatever confusion there is, of course, the document that has been loaded, so the number of that document is not just the one map, but on page 2 we find the other map. So we should --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we should identify clearly that -- so the number just assigned was just to the first page of that document. That's now on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is exactly wanted what I wanted to ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is now on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that the way that Your Honours would -- I think -- I think that's clearer if we do it that way, give it two separate numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's fine. But if you call for a certain document with a certain 65 ter number, then of course Madam Registrar gets the whole of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So unless there is a clear indication that only part of that document should be assigned a number we ask for, then of course the whole of the document gets it. So therefore -- but it's now clear. It's just the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honours, for that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us about your -- you started to tell us about your visit to Rznic, and you've mentioned the location of a rapid intervention unit there. Do you know who was in charge or who the commander of this rapid intervention unit was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I visited the place, the commander of the rapid intervention unit was Togeri.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that the first time - now, I'm talking about what was in your mind - as far as you were concerned, was that the first time you had met him?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes. The first time I met him was in Irzniq, yes, but I was told I had also met him in Tirana, but I didn't remember it from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I met Togeri, he told me that we had already met in Tirana once. Of course probably we had met, because many people came and went, but I couldn't remember all of them of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. And did this rapid intervention unit have any -- did they wear any particular sort of uniform?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I visited them, they had black uniforms and weapons that were somewhat better than the weapons that the other had. It was a very short time, though, it was only 15 minutes that I stayed there at this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And who introduced you to Toger or Togeri?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Ramush introduced me to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you -- were you provided with any information as to whether this rapid -- rapid intervention unit was part of any larger military grouping?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: From what I could observe there on the spot, this was a very -- a small group, a unit, but, as I told you, this was the time of the re-organisation of the army. So I don't know when the unit was formed -- formed exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. That might be when it was -- you may not know when it was formed, but my question is: As far as you're aware, was it part of any larger military grouping in the area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The rapid intervention unit was at the level of the local command. The rapid intervention unit were led by the zone commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when you say "local command," just be a little more precise if you wouldn't mind. What exactly are you referring to when you say that the rapid intervention unit was at the level of the local command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Rapid intervention unit in Dukagjin and in other areas were under the command of the zone commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Which zone commanders do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question? You mean which in plural or who in singular?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, which -- you say that the rapid intervention unit that you -- in Dukadjin and in other areas were under the command of the zone commanders. I'm asking you about this rapid intervention unit in Rznic. Was that rapid intervention unit in Rznic part of any military grouping in the Dukadjini area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Under the command of the Dukagjini Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. If you just look back at the map that I think you see -- should still be on the screen before you. You've told the Trial Chamber of travelling to these areas with -- I think you said that Mr. Haradinaj was with you some of the time at least. Okay --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, the places I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When you moved from one village to another, were you in company with KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Every time we were accompanied by KLA soldiers, especially my movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. And were they armed and escorting you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, of course they were armed and I was armed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. But these visits occurred during the day, the visits to the anti-aircraft gun emplacements and also the villages that we see mentioned there, Rznic, Prilep, Saptej, occurred during the day?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you travel by vehicle, or was it a combination of vehicle and travelling on foot, or something else?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes. We went to some of the places by car; some other places on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You earlier mentioned or started to mention that you went to this area of Reka e Keqe and that you've shown us the path that you took, which we can see on the dotted line on that particular exhibit. How did you travel from Gllogjan to the area of Reka e Keqe?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: From Gllogjan when we took this dotted line, we were travelling on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who is "we"? Who precisely are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: At that time I went to visit Reka e Keqe, I was together with Sali Veseli, but also a group of soldiers who accompanied us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who provided you with those soldiers that -- where did they come from is perhaps a clearer question?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I took these soldiers from Gllogjan, from the commander of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who? Who precisely?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Ramush, from Ramush. They would escort us towards Reka e Keqe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was their role, I take it, to provide you with protection and escort you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And this particular trip into the area of Reka e Keqe was done entirely on foot?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: In the territory of Reka e Keqe, we went to some places by car, but to some other places by foot, depending on the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. At this stage, I'm only just talking about -- have a drink if you've got -- if your throat's a bit sore, Mr. Zyrapi, and clear your throat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I don't know whether you are about to explore that area further, then we'd like to have a break first; if, however, you just finish --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, that would actually suit me because I can then finalise the business relating to the statements and make sure that that -- I'm going to get through that more smoothly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break and adjourn and resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I wonder if, just before I do, just on a matter of timing for tomorrow, I know my colleagues were concerned about when to next bring in the next witness, and I'll probably be about another 20 minutes, 25 minutes I would say with this witness. And I wonder if Mr. Emmerson or indeed all Defence counsel give us an idea, even a vague idea would be helpful about how long they will be with this witness so we can time bringing in the next gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, and other Defence counsel, could you give us an impression?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would have thought something in the region of about two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for you or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's what I had in mind for myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I contemplate between 20 and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I imagine something in the region of 20 minutes, depending on my colleagues, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's very useful, and I'll make sure that my colleagues are informed of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would altogether take approximately two sessions, but let's also see how much time we still need on the documents, et cetera. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you were talking earlier in your evidence about this trip that you made to the area of Reka e Keqe. Did you travel there, as you've said, on foot during the day or at night?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: During the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Because Serb forces were positioned along the road Prizren-Gjakove-Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown 65 ter what was 1306 page 2, the second page of the -- of the -- that formerly two-page exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's a map and it will have marked at the top of it "Annex B" side of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P120, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I wonder if the bottom left-hand quadrant could be -- yeah. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Witness, firstly, are those your markings?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, you see a dotted line. Going from Glodjane down to a place called Smolice. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that the path that you took to get to this area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It represents the route I took up to Reka e Keqe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you can see, obviously, that the road from Decani heading southwards towards Djakovica, you see three round circles on that road. What do those round circles represent?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: These circles represent the positions of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who provided you with intelligence or information as to the position of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I received the information from Sali Veseli. He had information where the Serb forces were along this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know if they were fixed positions?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: I don't know, but that's what I was told, that the Serb forces were positioned there during the time I was visiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And it would seem that your path necessarily involved crossing the road. Was that dangerous?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, of course it was dangerous because we were passing through an area where there were Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. You've mentioned some of the precautionary measures, one of which was travelling at night. And was the provision of this escort also designed to make sure -- well, designed to protect you from any Serb attack?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You -- did you successfully cross the road and -- without any -- being subjected to any attack from Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you eventually make it into the Reka e Keqe area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Into what area did you mean? Maybe -- can we clarify that on the-- at the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- because the interrupted line in fact does not go to Smolice, which was mentioned in your initial question. And therefore, I'm a little lost with the end of that trip. Maybe can you clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Yes. That's -- I think Your Honour's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where did you actually travel to? What was the name of the village that you travelled to?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: We travelled at night, as I said. We arrived at about 2.00 or 3.00 a.m. First of all, we arrived at Ramoc village. We were there at dawn and Naim Maloku came later. With him we went to the village of Smolice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. The map that you can see on the screen before you also has, apart from the dotted line showing your path, another dotted line enclosing an area in which you can see showing the initials NM and other initials, AH. What area is designated? What area is that area that's enclosed, including Junik and -- Junik and -- clearly Junik?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, the initials NM mean Naim Maloku where he was at the staff in Smolice and also AH, which is Aziz Hyseni in Smolice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was Aziz Hyseni, precisely?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In Junik not Smolice, the second one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Aziz was the commander of the staff in Junik at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was the overall point, the purpose of your travelling to this area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: The aim of my visit to this area was this: First of all, to visit the area and to acquaint ourselves with the units that were in the area, and also to incorporate the units of this area in the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in the area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: As I said, I arrived early in the morning and I stayed all day. This was the third day. I visited, I toured the area. And then I was told that in Rahovec there had been an attack by the Serb forces. At the end of the day I left; I followed the same path towards Gllogjan and then to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you return to Gllogjan at night?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise it was impossible to pass during the day. So I left at night. But when I arrived there at about 11.00 p.m., when -- in Gllogjan, then Ramush told me that I had to go to Rahovec. He gave me a car, by which I went to Jabllanice --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: -- where Lahi Brahimaj was waiting for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio. Have you inquired into when this three-days tour took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, the evidence we have so far is mid-July I believe. I don't think there's anything more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, can you help His Honour. You've mentioned mid-July for this visit. Have you got any -- can you offer any more precision than that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: This was a time I went. It was mid-July, and this was the third day of my tour in the area of Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- and following which you then left the area to go to Orahovac where there were reports of fighting breaking out. Is that -- do I understand your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now I want to return to Reka e Keqe. You've told us that your purpose was to speak -- to -- I think unify commands and incorporate this area. With -- which command in particular did you want to unify?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: With command of the local staff in Junik, to join it with the Dukagjini Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you speak to Aziz Hyseni and Naim Maloku about that very topic and about that proposal. Just tell us if you did or didn't?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, I did talk with them regarding the purpose of my visit to that territory. They agreed to join the command of Dukagjini Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that -- was it the view of the KLA General Staff that that should occur?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had you spoken to Ramush Haradinaj about that; and if so, had he expressed any views?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, I had spoken with him, and his view was that they -- these staffs should be incorporated under the operational zone staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was that eventually accomplished? Was this area of Reka e Keqe incorporated into the Dukadjin -- the command of the Dukadjini Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know the exact time of this joining or merger because of the poor communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's -- I want to return again to the -- to your visit into the Reka e Keqe area?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I wonder if that last -- the last two words of that last answer might be explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It will -- in fact, that's a topic that I fully intend to cover --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But I'd like to proceed in my own way if I may and we'll deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Naim Maloku was right down south in the Reka e Keqe area, and Aziz Hyseni was up north in that area in Junik. How did you get from Ramoc up to Junik to speak to Aziz Hyseni?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: From Smolice together with Naim Maloku, we went by car to Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you have your escort of soldiers with you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you travelled during the day up there and had -- conferred with Aziz Hyseni?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you travel back to Ramoc again, that day?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, we travelled back on the same day in the evening, and then we continued our way on foot to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. That's what I wanted to know. Did you actually retrace your steps, so to speak, back to Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You earlier, in answer, mentioned some --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned -- you made a reference to "poor communication." Can you tell us what the communication was like between this area of Reka e Keqe - and I'm talking in military terms now of course - between Reka e Keqe and the Dukadjini Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: At the time that I visited it, it was difficult to communicate because it was impossible to have direct communication or through courier. The courier had to pass through all this territory, which was rife in perils. And I didn't observe communication through radios, Motorola or other means of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would a courier have faced the same problem you did in getting from the Gllogjan area to Reka e Keqe and vice versa; namely, the Serb positions on that road?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned that when you got back to the Gllogjan area, Lahi Brahimaj was there. What --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's not a correct statement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: After you crossed the road, the road leading down to Djakovica, did you -- where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: After I returned, I went back to Gllogjan, and there I met Ramush. He gave me a car to go to Jabllanice. And then I was called by the General Staff to go to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think you -- who did you see in Jablanica? Which personalities did you meet in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: In Jabllanice, I met Lahi Brahimaj, who was waiting for us to convey to me the order of the General Staff to go back; and in his car, we went to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And was that by pre-arrangement? Did you -- did you go to Jablanica intending to meet Lahi Brahimaj, or was it purely by accident?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: To meet him and to continue together on our path, on our way to the General Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- very unfortunate misprint at line 11 on page 83, the order of the General Staff was actually what the witness said, and Your Honours can see what is and should not be there. I thought I should stop that right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that it's a sensitive expression, of course, in this context. It will be corrected. Attention is asked specifically of those who are correcting the transcript, page 83, line 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You still haven't really clarified it as clearly as I would like it to be clarified, please. When you're travelling towards Jablanica, was it in your mind, did you intend, to meet up with Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, how did that come about? Why -- why was that your plan and how did that come to be your plan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Lahi Brahimaj was a member of the General Staff, and he had received orders that we go back to the General Staff, who was -- which was located in Rahovec for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That may be so, that may be so, but why and how did it come about that you intended to catch up with, meet with, Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: As I said earlier, the order given by the General Staff was to return because of the fighting going on in Rahovec. And the person who brought this order from the General Staff was Lahi Brahimaj, who was waiting for us in Jabllanice. After I returned from Reka e Keqe zone, I went to Gllogjan. There Ramush Haradinaj told us to go back to Rahovec. And then he gave -- lended me a car and escorted me up to Jabllanice -- which escorted me up to Jabllanice. I met Lahi Brahimaj, he gave me the order, and together we went to Rahovec, where the General Staff was located at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the time that you were touring during this tour of three days, other than the Serb positions that you've mentioned, did you encounter any other Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: When I toured Prilep village, the road was -- which goes to Decane-Gjakove was nearby and the Serbian forces had taken up positions there, but not in the hinterland of the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you some statements, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown - I've got now hard copies and also from e-court - the -- we'll deal perhaps first with the November 2005 statement, that's 65 ter 1308, and perhaps if I may have the assistance of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we earlier assigned already a number to the November 2005 statement, so I take it that then this one will replace, Madam Registrar, the earlier one. Yes. That's confirmed. Has it been uploaded in e-court, Mr. Di Fazio? I see Madam Registrar is nodding yes, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And -- yes. This is now the November 2005 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I would like to produce hard copies for the -- for the benefit of the witness. I've got hard copies of the Albanian version and the -- and the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, do you recognise your signature anywhere on that document that's -- you're advised to look at the English, I think.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You also have an Albanian version of the statement. Could you just have a quick -- quick look at that and so that you can acquaint yourself with this particular statement, the translation. Now, do you recall giving that statement to the officers of the OTP, the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, I have given the statement to the OTP in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. And does that contain information which you would provide again if questioned about those topics in that statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender the statement, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since there are no objections, the -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English being the original one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I would now like to show the April 2007 statement to Mr. Zyrapi, and also produce to him the hard copies of the English and the Albanian versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P121, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'd just like to basically repeat all the same questions that I put to you in relation to the other statement; namely, can you identify the statement, just refresh your memory, as to see -- in order to see which statement it is? Look at the signatures, and then can you tell us if that statement contains material that you would provide to this Chamber if you were asked questions about those topics?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature and I will, as you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, two annexed maps we made now two different exhibits, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, the maps are tendered separately from -- they were once part of the statement, but they've now gone in separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Di Fazio, let's have a look at what you are providing to us at this moment. That's the April 2007. Let me just have a look again at the e-mail. "Oral evidence will be led of the material referred to in paragraphs 1 to 11." I see that -- or am I at the wrong one now? Let's just have a look. I'm afraid I'm at the wrong one. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've been assured it's been correctly redacted this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look. No, this is the April statement. I think I've got the -- do I have the right one? Yes. No, I see it's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please, that now leaves the question of the -- the exhibits. I -- I think in this -- from the point of view of speed and efficiency, if all of the documents referred to in the statement, the 2007 statement, can, at the very least, be marked for identification. The issue of their full admissibility is a matter that the parties can address to you in -- perhaps in written form, perhaps by way of motion, if necessary. And there may be and it may be, as Mr. Emmerson pointed out to you, there may be no -- no problems with a good number of those -- of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has Madam Registrar a list of those documents so that she -- are these the numbers we find on the pages -- I mean, would that be sufficient for Madam Registrar to -- of the numbers we find in paragraph 48 of the April statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've provided a spreadsheet, if Your Honours please, that will enable connections to be made for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Apparently that bears the number -- the spreadsheet that I've prepared bears the number 65 ter 1305. Now, I don't need to tender that into -- into evidence. That's just a spreadsheet. It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Just to assist Madam Registrar, we could later --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- check on the basis of the list of documents marked for identification. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, then I take it that the Defence would agree that Madam Registrar takes her time to have it all properly noted?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I have no difficulty with that, and on the assumption that no issue is taken as between a facsimile stamp of the signature and the signature itself, then -- then I have no difficulty with this witness being used as the vehicle through which those documents are marked for identification and, if appropriate, tendered. I'm making that assumption because I don't suppose he was in a position to identify the difference between the one and the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, unless he has seen the originals, I do not know. Mr. Di Fazio, has the witness been shown, when he commented on it, copies or has he been shown -- and apart from that, stamps have the advantage of usually being the same all the time without any variation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The witness -- the witness made reference to stamps in the 2007 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In fact, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a different reference in a different context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, for example, if you find us this comment: "This document contains the long and short version of Ramush Haradinaj's signature."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the witness then seen the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, so on -- that means that -- is there any document where the -- where the Office of the Prosecution assumes that the witness says anything more than that: This signature, as found in a copy of a document, is a signature the witness identifies as the same also what he knows to be Mr. Haradinaj's signature? I mean, is there any -- any moment where the Prosecution would like to use this evidence as to say that Mr. Haradinaj personally signed the document rather than that a stamp with his signature has been put on that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, not on the basis of this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All he can say is this -- I recognise the signature, the long and the short versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, whether -- I don't think he goes so far as to say as to how that came to be placed there, whether it was by human hand or whether it was by mechanism of a stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But he does recognise the long and the short signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it's perfectly clear what -- what the extent is to which this proves anything at all. Mr. Guy-Smith, Mr. Harvey, do you take a similar position as the Haradinaj Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, with regard to any issues concerning signatures there, I don't know to what extent there is going to be any reliance on some of the commentary in which there was interpretative remarks made concerning some of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is -- I think it's a comment on which you could cross-examine the witness. It's -- it's 92 ter testimony at this moment. Very often it just says: I recognise the signature. But if it's more, then of course it's what the witness, under 92 ter, has --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
